page: Vultr vhf-6c-24gb is an x86_64 architecture virtual server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It features 6 shared vCPUs mapped to 3 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 448 GB local NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present on this instance type.

Benchmark results show average single-core and multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1670.29 and a multi-core score of 9438.87. Single-threaded gzip compression is a notable strength, reaching 33.56 GB/sec. However, memory bandwidth exhibits significant bottlenecks under large workloads, dropping to a weak 26.11 GB/sec for read-only large blocks and a poor 13.1 GB/sec for write large blocks. Geekbench multi-core performance is also weak at 4090.0, and static web serving throughput is limited to 6.1 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and weak large-block memory bandwidth, this server is best suited for general-purpose workloads that do not require sustained, high-throughput memory operations. It performs adequately for software compilation, text processing, and light database operations, as reflected by its average Geekbench compiling score of 5967.0 and 7.25 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It is not recommended for memory-intensive applications, large-scale LLM inference, or heavy multi-threaded database systems.
description: The Vultr vhf-6c-24gb is an x86_64 virtual server from the High Frequency Compute family, configured with 6 shared Intel vCPUs, 24.0 GB of RAM, and a 448 GB local NVMe SSD. It delivers average single-core performance, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core score of 1670.29 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 33.56 GB/sec. However, it exhibits performance trade-offs, particularly in memory bandwidth, where large-block write speeds are poor at 13.1 GB/sec, and multi-core Geekbench scores are weak at 4090.0. Lacking a GPU, it is unsuitable for heavy parallel processing or large language model inference. This server is best utilized for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, and moderate web serving where resource demands are balanced and do not saturate memory bandwidth.
